47.s: Who is the foremost composer of Carnatic music?
47.x:
Saint Thyagaraja (1767–1847) is regarded as one of the greatest composers of Carnatic music and is revered as a member of the Carnatic Trinity, along with Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri. He composed thousands of devotional Kritis, most of them dedicated to Lord Rama. His compositions are known for their profound devotion, musical excellence and philosophical depth, making them central to the Carnatic music tradition. Although Annamacharya composed over 32,000 Sankirtanas in praise of Lord Venkateswara and is regarded as the Padakavita Pitamaha, the title of the foremost composer of Carnatic music is associated with Saint Thyagaraja. His annual Thyagaraja Aradhana at Tiruvaiyaru continues to attract musicians from across the world. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• Foremost Composer of Carnatic Music – Saint Thyagaraja
• Carnatic Trinity – Thyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, Syama Sastri
• Devotional Deity – Lord Rama

47.s: Who was the pioneer composer of the kriti form of Carnatic music?
47.x: Annamacharya, the prolific 15th-century composer of Telugu devotional songs (sankirtanas) at Tirumala, is regarded as the pioneer of the kriti form that later flourished with composers like Thyagaraja, having predated and influenced the classical Carnatic kriti tradition.

47.s: Who recovered and edited Annamacharya's sankirtanas preserved on copper plates at Tirumala?
47.x: Veturi Prabhakara Sastry recovered and edited the copper-plate songs; C.P. Brown is linked with Vemana.
xa: Veturi said Annamacharya **created the science of sankirtana**.
**Annamayya district** is named after him.

47.s: "Padakavita Pitamaha" is a title of:
47.x: Padakavita Pitamaha, Sankirtanacharya and Harikirtanacharya are titles of Annamacharya.
xa: China Tirumalacharya was the **eldest son of Peda Tirumalacharya**; he wrote **Sankirtana Lakshanamu**.
Praise: "**Right hand to Telugu words**" (Puttaparthi Narayanacharyulu); "**Incarnated Telugu**" (Arudra).

47.s: Annamacharya is known in Telugu literary history as the:
o: Author of the first Telugu Dandakam
Father of the Telugu keertana and pioneer of padakavita
First translator of the Ramayana into Telugu
Founder of the Sanskrit court epic tradition
47.x: Annamacharya is regarded as the father of the Telugu keertana and a pioneer of the padakavita or pada form.
47.tq: Identify the exact literary contribution rather than a related but incorrect achievement.
xs: Annamacharya is the **Father of the Telugu keertana** and **pioneer of padakavita** — option **(2)**.
The first Telugu **Dandakam** is **Potana's Bhogini Dandakam**; the first woman Ramayana translator is **Molla**.
xa: His **Sri Venkateswara Satakam** = first Telugu **Shringara Satakam**.
⚠ Sri Venkateswara Satakam is **Annamacharya's**, not Pedda Tirumalacharya's.

47.s: Annamacharya, the composer of sankirtanas on Lord Venkateswara, was a contemporary of which ruler?
47.x: Annamacharya (1408-1503) was a contemporary of Saluva Narasimha (APPSC-G2 2011). Pedakomati Vema Reddy was Srinatha's patron, Abul Hasan Tana Shah imprisoned Bhakta Ramadasu, and Krishnadevaraya is not the ruler linked with Annamacharya.
xs: Annamacharya (**1408-1503**) was a contemporary of **Saluva Narasimha** (APPSC-G2 2011) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Pedakomati Vema Reddy** was **Srinatha's** patron at Kondaveedu, not Annamacharya's.
**Abul Hasan Tana Shah** imprisoned **Bhakta Ramadasu** in Golconda fort.
xa: Annamacharya was met by the Kannada saint **Purandara Dasa**.
Some notes give his dates as **1424-1508**.
**Annamayya district** is named after Annamacharya of **Tallapaka**.

47.s: Kshetrayya is associated with which form of composition?
47.x: Kshetrayya is associated with padams; Tallapaka is linked with sankirtana.
xa: Andhra's contributions: Dvaita at **Srikurmam**, **Aradhya Saivism**, **Tallapaka sankirtana**, **Bhadrachalam (Ramadasu)**, **Kshetrayya's padams**.
**Aradhya Saivism** was founded by **Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya**; it kept Vedic learning and varna while preaching Shiva bhakti.
**Dvaita** (dualism) is the philosophy of **Madhvacharya**.

47.s: Annamacharya composed his sankirtanas primarily in praise of:
47.x: Annamacharya composed about 32,000 sankirtanas to Lord Venkateswara.
47.tq: Use the deity association to distinguish Annamacharya from other devotional composers.
xs: Annamacharya's sankirtanas were to **Lord Venkateswara** of **Tirumala** — option **(2)**.
He composed about **32,000**; only about **12,000** survive.
**Rama** was the deity of **Ramadasu** and **Tyagaraja**; **Krishna** (Muvva Gopala) of **Kshetrayya**.
xa: Born at **Tallapaka**; dates **1408-1503**.
Contemporary ruler: **Saluva Narasimha** (APPSC-G2 **2011**).

47.s: Bhakta Ramadasu's Dasarathi Satakam was translated into English by
47.x: Dr. Bhanumathi Ramakrishna translated Dasarathi Satakam into English (APPSC-G2 2001). C.P. Brown translated Vemana's verses, Veturi Prabhakara Sastry recovered Annamacharya's copper-plate songs, and Arudra called Annamacharya 'Incarnated Telugu'.
xs: **Dr. Bhanumathi Ramakrishna** translated the Dasarathi Satakam into English (APPSC-G2 2001) — option **(3)** is correct.
**C.P. Brown** translated **Vemana's** verses (**1829**).
**Veturi Prabhakara Sastry** recovered Annamacharya's **copper-plate songs**; **Arudra** called Annamacharya **"Incarnated Telugu"**.
xa: Ramadasu wrote the Dasarathi Satakam **in prison** in **Golconda fort**.
Ramadasu = **Kancharla Gopanna**, nephew of **Akkanna and Madanna**.

47.s: About how many sankirtanas did Annamacharya compose?
47.x: Annamacharya composed about 32,000 sankirtanas, of which about 12,000 survive on copper plates.

47.s: Who called Annamacharya 'Incarnated Telugu'?
47.x: Arudra called Annamacharya 'Incarnated Telugu'; Veturi Prabhakara Sastry edited his copper-plate songs.

47.s: Annamacharya was born at:
47.x: Annamacharya was born at Tallapaka; Bammera is Potana's native place and Movva Kshetrayya's.

47.s:
Consider the following statements about Annamacharya:
1. He was a contemporary of Saluva Narasimha.
2. He was a contemporary of Tyagaraja.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
47.x: Annamacharya was a contemporary of Saluva Narasimha; he preceded Tyagaraja and was not his contemporary.

47.s: Who was the composer of " Subhadra Kalyanam "?
47.x: Tallapaka Thimmakka, an early Telugu poetess associated with the Tallapaka family of composers (linked to Annamacharya's lineage), is credited as the composer of ' Subhadra Kalyanam '.

47.s: Peda Tirumalacharya, author of Vairagya Vachanamalika, was Annamacharya's:
47.x: Peda Tirumalacharya was Annamacharya's son; his works include Vairagya Vachanamalika and Sudarshana Ragada.
xa: Peda Tirumalacharya's other works: **Sankirtanas**, **Seesa padya satakam**, **Sudarshana Ragada**, **Chakravala Manjari**.
⚠ **Trap:** **Sri Venkateswara Satakam** is **Annamacharya's**, not Pedda Tirumalacharya's.

47.s: Who held the title Ashtabhasha Kavi Chakravarti?
47.x: China Tirumalacharya, Annamacharya's grandson, held the title and wrote the Ashtabhasha Dandakam.
xa: He also wrote **Sankirtana Lakshanamu**.
⚠ **Trap:** Do not credit China Tirumalayya with the **first Telugu Dandakam** — that was Potana's **Bhogini Dandakam**.

47.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
47.x: Timmakka, the wife of Annamacharya, wrote Subhadra Kalyanam in Telugu.
47.tq: Start from the sure poet–work pair and reject swapped literary associations.
xs: **Timmakka — Subhadra Kalyanam** is correctly matched — option **(3)** is correct.
**Tirumalamba** wrote **Varadambika Parinayam**; **Raghunathabhyudayam** is **Ramabhadramba's**.
**Gangadevi** wrote **Madhura Vijayam**, not Varadambika Parinayam.
xa: **Timmakka** (Tirumalamma) was **Annamacharya's first wife** and the **first woman poet** of the Andhra region.
**Subhadra Kalyanam** (Subhadra Parinayam) is a **Dvipada kavya**.

47.s: The first Telugu Dandakam, the Bhogini Dandakam, was written by:
47.x: The first Telugu Dandakam was Potana's Bhogini Dandakam.
xa: **Bhogini Dandakam** is about **Sarvajna Singabhupala** and **Bhogini**.
Other FIRSTs: **Sri Venkateswara Satakam** (Annamacharya) = first Telugu **Shringara Satakam**; **Vrushadhipa Satakam** = first full-featured satakam.
**Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya** = originator of the **Sataka form** in Telugu.

47.s: Sri Venkateswara Satakam, regarded as the first Telugu Shringara Satakam, was written by
47.x: Sri Venkateswara Satakam is Annamacharya's work and the first Telugu Shringara Satakam. Crediting it to his son Peda Tirumalacharya is the common trap; China Tirumalacharya wrote Ashtabhasha Dandakam and Chinnanna wrote Annamacharya Charitra.
47.tq: Venkateswara Satakam = Annamacharya, not Pedda Tirumalacharya.
xs: **Sri Venkateswara Satakam**, the first Telugu Shringara Satakam, was written by **Annamacharya** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ Crediting it to his son **Peda Tirumalacharya** is the common trap.
**China Tirumalacharya** wrote Ashtabhasha Dandakam; **Chinnanna** wrote Annamacharya Charitra.
xa: Annamacharya's other Telugu works: **Sringara Manjari** (**258 dvipadas**), **Dvipada Ramayanam**, **Alivelumangamma Satakam**.
His Sanskrit works: **Sankirtana Lakshanam**, **Venkatachala Mahatyam**.

47.s: Annamacharya Charitra, the Dvipada biography of Annamacharya, was written by:
47.x: Chinnanna (Tiruvenkatanatha), a grandson of Annamacharya, wrote Annamacharya Charitra.

47.s: Tallapaka Timmakka is remembered as the:
o: First Telugu woman to translate the Ramayana
47.x: Timmakka, Annamacharya's wife, is the first woman poet of Andhra; Molla was the first woman translator of the Ramayana.

47.s: Who wrote Veerabhadra Vijayam?
47.x: Bammera Potana wrote Veerabhadra Vijayam, Bhogini Dandakam and Andhra Mahabhagavatam.

47.s: Veerabhadra Vijayam, written at the request of Ivaturi Somanaradhya, is regarded as the first work of:
47.x: The cited accounts regard Veerabhadra Vijayam as Potana's first work, written at the request of his guru Ivaturi Somanaradhya.
xa: Potana's other works: **Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu**, **Bhogini Dandakam**, **Narayana Satakam** (lost).
Potana's title: **Sahaja Panditudu**.

47.s: Potana dedicated his Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu to:
47.x: The Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu, the Telugu Bhagavata Purana, was offered to Lord Rama; Potana wrote eight of its twelve skandhas.
xa: Other skandhas: **Bopparaju Gangana** (5th), **Erchuri Singana** (6th), **Veligandala Narayana** (11th-12th).
**C.P. Brown** printed Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu in **1840**.
Potana vowed **never to dedicate his work to a human king**.

47.s: Which one of the following pairs of titles is associated with Bammera Potana?
47.x: Potana was known by the titles Sahaja Panditudu and Nigarva Chudamani.
47.tq: Use exact title-pair recognition to eliminate titles belonging to other poets.
xs: Potana's titles were **Sahaja Panditudu** and **Nigarva Chudamani** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Andhra Kavita Pitamaha** is **Allasani Peddana's** title; **Padakavita Pitamaha** is **Annamacharya's**.
**Kavibrahma** is **Tikkana's** title.
xa: Potana (c. **1450-1510**) was a native of **Bammera** (Janagama district, Telangana).
He was a contemporary of **Srinatha** (Kavi Sarvabhauma); some notes make him Srinatha's brother-in-law.
Other titles: **Nannaya** = Adikavi; **Errapragada** = Prabandha Parameswara.

47.s: Bammera Potana refused to dedicate his work to which ruler?
47.x: Potana vowed never to dedicate his work to a human king, refused Sarvajna Singabhupala of Rachakonda and offered the Bhagavatam to Sri Rama.

47.s: Of the 12 skandhas of the Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu, how many did Potana write?
47.x: Potana wrote 8 of the 12 skandhas; others such as Bopparaju Gangana and Erchuri Singana completed the rest.

47.s: Potana's Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu was printed by C.P. Brown in:
47.x: C.P. Brown printed the Bhagavatamu in 1840; his Verses of Vemana came out in 1829.

47.s: Who said that paper has been used for writing in the 15th century?
47.x:
Srinatha, one of the greatest Telugu poets of the 15th century, mentions the use of paper as a writing material in his literary works. His references indicate that by the fifteenth century, paper had gradually begun replacing palm leaves for literary and administrative purposes in parts of South India. These literary references are valuable historical evidence for tracing the introduction and spread of paper in medieval Andhra. Hence, the correct answer is Option (3).
Exam Note:
• Earliest literary reference to paper in Telugu – Srinatha
• Period – 15th Century

47.s: Srinatha served as Vidyadhikari (education minister) at the court of
47.x: Srinatha was Vidyadhikari at the Kondaveedu court of Pedakomati Vema Reddy and wrote the king's Sanskrit inscriptions. Under Veerabhadra Reddy at Rajahmundry he wrote Bhimakhandam and Kasikhandam; at Devaraya II's court he won the title Kavi Sarvabhauma; Sarvajna Singabhupala is linked with Potana's refusal of patronage.
xs: Srinatha was **Vidyadhikari** under **Pedakomati Vema Reddy of Kondaveedu** — option **(3)** (APPSC **2001/2002**).
He also wrote the king's **Sanskrit inscriptions**.
**Veerabhadra Reddy** = Rajahmundry phase; **Devaraya II** = Kavi Sarvabhauma; **Sarvajna Singabhupala** = Potana's refused patron.
xa: Kondaveedu fell in **1424**.
Haravilasamu describes **Reddi-era sea trade**.

47.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Rajahmundry — Veerabhadra Reddy through Bendapudi Anantamatya
47.x: After Kondaveedu fell in 1424, Srinatha went to Rajahmundry under Veerabhadra Reddy through Bendapudi Anantamatya. The other pairs confuse patrons or places.
47.tq: Start with the court–patron pair and reject swapped rulers and locations.
xs: **Rajahmundry — Veerabhadra Reddy, through Bendapudi Anantamatya** — option **(2)**.
**Kondaveedu** = **Pedakomati Vema Reddy**; **Vijayanagara** = **Devaraya II**.
xa: At Rajahmundry he wrote **Bhimakhandam** and **Kasikhandam**.
Haravilasamu was dedicated to **Avachi Tippaya Setti**.

47.s: Which statement about Srinatha is correct?
o: He pioneered the Prabandha style, and his age is known as the Kavya Yuga.
He founded the Tallapaka tradition of sankirtana.
He was the composer of the Pancharatna Kritis.
He was the first Telugu woman poet and composed Bhogini Dandakam.
47.x: Srinatha is regarded as a pioneer of the Prabandha style, and his period is called the Kavya Yuga. The other statements refer to different literary or musical figures.
47.tq: Identify the correct literary contribution among cross-period distractors.
xs: Srinatha **pioneered the Prabandha style**; his age is the **Kavya Yuga** — option **(1)**.
**Tallapaka sankirtana** = **Annamacharya**; **Pancharatna kritis** = **Tyagaraja**; **Bhogini Dandakam** = **Potana**; first woman poet = **Timmakka**.
xa: He wrote **more kavyas than any other Telugu poet**.
Title: **Kavi Sarvabhauma**.

47.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding Srinatha's works and their dedications?
47.x: Sringara Naishadhamu was dedicated to the minister Mamidi, or Madiki, Singana. Haravilasamu was dedicated to Avachi Tippaya Setti, while Sivaratri Mahatmyam was dedicated to Mummadi Santayya.
47.tq: Start from the sure author–dedication pair and eliminate the swapped patrons.
xs: **Sringara Naishadhamu — Mamidi Singana** is correct — option **(2)**.
**Haravilasamu** — **Avachi Tippaya Setti**; **Sivaratri Mahatmyam** — **Mummadi Santayya**.
**Bhimakhandamu** was written at **Veerabhadra Reddy**'s Rajahmundry court.
xa: **Kasikhandamu** was also dedicated to **Madiki Singana**.
Sivaratri Mahatmyam tells the story of the Brahmin **Sukumara**.

47.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Srinatha's Haravilasamu?
o: It was dedicated to Avachi Tippaya Setti
It is chiefly a source on the military organisation of the Vijayanagara Empire
It describes Reddi-period sea trade, including imports and exports
47.x: Haravilasamu, dedicated to Avachi Tippaya Setti, is valued as a source on Reddi-period sea trade, imports and exports, not on Vijayanagara military organisation.

47.s: After the fall of Rajahmundry, Srinatha's chatu verses chiefly portrayed which condition?
o: The maritime wealth of Avachi Tippaya Setti
The religious debates at the Vijayanagara court
The prosperity of the Gajapati court
The hard life and coarse food of poverty-stricken Palnadu
47.x: After Rajahmundry fell in 1448, Srinatha lived in poverty in Palnadu. His chatu verses provide a literary picture of its hardship and coarse food.
47.tq: Connect a biographical event with the social content of the poet’s verses.
xs: Srinatha's chatu verses portray the **hard life and coarse food of poverty-stricken Palnadu** — option **(4)**.
He lived in poverty there after **Rajahmundry fell (1448)**.
**Avachi Tippaya Setti**'s sea trade is in **Haravilasamu**, not the chatu verses.
xa: Later he found refuge with **Santhalingayya** of the Bhikshavritti matha at **Srisailam**.
⚠ Kondaveedu fell **1424**; Rajahmundry fell **1448**.

47.s: Srinatha received the title Kavi Sarvabhauma at the court of:
47.x: At Vijayanagara Srinatha defeated Gauda Dindima Bhatta before Devaraya II and won Kanakabhishekam and the title Kavi Sarvabhauma.

47.s: The first reference to paper as a writing material in Andhra is found in the works of:
47.x: Srinatha gives the first reference to paper as writing material in Andhra (APPSC 2012).

47.s: In the APPSC 2025 key, which work was treated as NOT written by Srinatha?
47.x: Haravilasam, Madanavilasa Bhanam and Sivaratri Mahatmyam are Srinatha's; the APPSC 2025 key made Palnati Veera Charitra the 'not by Srinatha' answer.

47.s: Srinatha dedicated Sringara Naishadhamu to:
47.x: Sringara Naishadhamu went to minister Mamidi (Madiki) Singana; Haravilasamu to Avachi Tippaya Setti and Sivaratri Mahatmyam to Mummadi Santayya.

47.s: Palnati Veera Charitra is a dvipada ballad of the Palnadu war fought in:
47.x: Palnati Veera Charitra describes the Palnadu war of 1182.

47.s: Srinatha moved to the Rajahmundry court after the fall of Kondaveedu in:
47.x: Kondaveedu fell in 1424 and Srinatha went to Veerabhadra Reddy at Rajahmundry; Rajahmundry itself fell in 1448.

47.s: Vemana's verses are mostly composed in which metre and commonly end with which refrain?
47.x: Vemana mainly used the Ataveladi metre, and his verses commonly conclude with the refrain “Vishwadabhirama Vinura Vema.”
47.tq: Pair the distinctive metre with its recurring refrain rather than recognising either in isolation.
xs: Vemana mostly used the **Ataveladi** metre with the refrain **"Vishwadabhirama Vinura Vema"** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Dvipada** is the metre of works like **Basava Puranam** and **Annamacharya Charitra**, not Vemana's verses.
xa: His verses are short, **satakam-style**, in **colloquial Telugu**.
**Dating disputed:** **17th c.** vs **14th-15th c.** — learn both.

47.s: Which one of the following best reflects the social message of Veerabrahmendra Swamy?
o: He condemned caste differences and accepted disciples across castes and faiths.
He rejected vernacular literature in favour of Sanskrit.
He supported ritual hierarchy as the basis of social order.
He defended caste distinctions and restricted discipleship to one community.
47.x: Veerabrahmendra Swamy strongly condemned caste differences and accepted disciples from different castes and faiths, including Siddaiah, a Muslim.
47.tq: Apply the reformer’s stated social principles to a concrete description.
xs: Veerabrahmendra Swamy **condemned caste differences** and **accepted disciples across castes and faiths** — option **(1)** is correct.
His disciple **Siddaiah** was a **Muslim**, so options (3) and (4) are the opposite of his message.
xa: His prophecies are in **Kalagnanam**.
He is paired with **Vemana** as Andhra's anti-caste voices.

47.s: Vemana's poetry is best known for:
o: criticism of caste, superstition and empty ritual
47.x: Vemana criticised superstition, empty ritual, idol worship and hypocrisy and advocated humanism and equality.
xa: **C.P. Brown** edited and translated his verses as **Verses of Vemana** (**1829**).
Vemana is paired with **Potuluri Veerabrahmam** as Andhra's **anti-caste voices**.

47.s: Who translated Vemana's verses into English as 'Verses of Vemana' (1829)?
47.x: C.P. Brown collected, edited and translated Vemana's verses, published in 1829.
xa: Refrain: **"Vishwadabhirama Vinura Vema"**.
⚠ C.P. Brown dates: Verses of Vemana **1829**; Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu **1840**.

47.s: The prophecies of Potuluri Veerabrahmendra Swamy are known as:
47.x: Veerabrahmendra Swamy's work is Kalagnanam, a book of prophecies.

47.s: Siddaiah, a famous disciple of Veerabrahmendra Swamy, was a:
47.x: Veerabrahmendra Swamy condemned caste and had disciples of all faiths, including Siddaiah, a Muslim.

47.s: Who translated Dasarathi Satakam into English?
47.x:
Dr. Bhanumati Ramakrishna, a distinguished scholar, translated the famous Telugu devotional work Dasarathi Satakam, composed by Kancherla Gopanna (Bhakta Ramadasu), into English. The translation helped introduce Telugu devotional literature to a wider national and international audience while preserving the literary beauty and spiritual essence of the original work. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Dasarathi Satakam → Kancherla Gopanna
• English Translation → Dr. Bhanumati Ramakrishna

47.s:
With reference to cultural history of India, consider the following statements:
1. Most of the Tyagaraja Kritis are devotional songs in praise of Lord Krishna.
2. Tyagaraja created several new ragas.
3. Annamacharya and Tyagaraja are contemporaries.
4. Annamacharya kirtanas are devotional songs in praise of Lord Venkateshwara.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
47.x: Tyagaraja was a renounced composer of Carnatic music, a form of Indian classical music. Tyagaraja and his contemporaries, Shyam Shastri and Muthuswami Dikshitai, were regarded as a trinity of Carnatic Music. Tyagaraja composed thousands of devotional compositions, most in Telugu and praise of Lord Rama. He created several new ragas. Annamacharya was a 15th century Hindu saint and is the earliest known Indian musician to compose songs called sankirtanas in praise of the God Venkateshwara, a form of Vishnu.

47.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Tirumala — Annamacharya and the Tallapaka family
47.x: Tirumala is associated with Annamacharya and the Tallapaka family. Bhadrachalam is associated with Ramadasu, Muvva with Kshetrayya, and Srikurmam with Narahari Tirtha.
47.tq: Start from the temple–saint pair that is most firmly associated and eliminate shifted pairings.
xs: **Tirumala — Annamacharya and the Tallapaka family** is correctly matched — option **(1)** is correct.
**Bhadrachalam = Ramadasu**, not Kshetrayya; **Muvva = Kshetrayya**, not Tyagaraja.
**Srikurmam = Narahari Tirtha**, who spread **Dvaita**.
xa: **Tiruvaiyaru** = **Tyagaraja**.
**Tarigonda Vengamamba** is also linked with **Tirumala**.

47.s: Dhurjati is associated with which work?
47.x: Dhurjati wrote Srikalahasteeswara Satakam, regarded as a foremost Shaiva satakam.
47.tq: Distinguish similarly named satakams by their author and deity.
xs: Dhurjati wrote the **Srikalahasteeswara Satakam**, the foremost **Shaiva satakam** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Venkateshwara Satakam** = **Annamacharya**; **Narayana Satakam** = **Potana** (lost); **Vrushadhipa Satakam** = **Palkuriki Somanatha**.
xa: **Vrushadhipa Satakam** = first Telugu satakam with all satakam features.
**Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya** = originator of the **Sataka form** in Telugu.

47.s: Which statement regarding Kshetrayya is correct?
o: He composed over a thousand Movva Gopala padams at Abdullah Qutb Shah’s court.
He wrote the Basava Puranam in Dwipada metre at the Kakatiya court.
He composed the Pancharatna kritis at Tiruvaiyaru.
47.x: Kshetrayya composed over a thousand Movva Gopala padams and is associated with Abdullah Qutb Shah’s court.
47.tq: Use the court–composer–work combination to separate closely related bhakti figures.
xs: Kshetrayya composed **over a thousand Movva Gopala padams** at **Abdullah Qutb Shah's court** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Srikalahasteeswara Satakam** = **Dhurjati**; **Basava Puranam** = **Palkuriki Somanatha**.
**Pancharatna kritis** at **Tiruvaiyaru** = **Tyagaraja**.
xa: His padams are **Shringara padams** to **Muvva Gopala** (Krishna).
⚠ Ramadasu = Golconda prison under **Tana Shah**; Kshetrayya = **Abdullah Qutb Shah's** court.

47.s: Bhakta Ramadasu (Kancharla Gopanna) used state revenue to rebuild the Rama temple at:
47.x: Ramadasu, a Golconda revenue official, rebuilt the Bhadrachalam Rama temple and was jailed by Tana Shah for 12 years.
xa: Bhakta Ramadasu = **Kancharla Gopanna**, born **1620** at **Nelakondapalli** (Khammam).
Guru **Raghunatha Bhattacharya**; nephew of **Akkanna and Madanna**.
He wrote **Dasarathi Satakam** in prison.

47.s: Which of the following works is associated with Bhakta Ramadasu?
47.x: Dasarathi Satakam, written in prison, and the Ramadasu kirtanas are associated with Bhakta Ramadasu.
47.tq: Match the devotional author with his literary work.
xs: **Dasarathi Satakam**, written in prison, is Bhakta Ramadasu's — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kalagnanam** = **Potuluri Veerabrahmam**; **Nalayira Divya Prabandham** = **Alvars**; **Molla Ramayanam** = **Molla**.
xa: He also composed the **Ramadasu kirtanas / keertanas**.
English translation of Dasarathi Satakam: **Dr. Bhanumathi Ramakrishna** (APPSC-G2 2001).

47.s: Tyagaraja is associated with which place?
47.x: Tyagaraja composed his Rama kritis at Tiruvaiyaru; Movva is Kshetrayya's and Bhadrachalam Ramadasu's.

47.s: Bhakta Ramadasu was imprisoned in Golconda fort for 12 years by:
47.x: Abul Hasan Tana Shah jailed Ramadasu for 12 years; Kshetrayya was at Abdullah Qutb Shah's court.

47.s: Tarigonda Vengamamba wrote Venkatachala Mahatyamu in praise of the deity of:
47.x: Vengamamba, an 18th-century poet, sang of Venkateswara of Tirumala in Venkatachala Mahatyamu.

47.s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the Carnatic Trinity?
47.x: The Carnatic Trinity is Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Shyama Shastri; Annamacharya was earlier and not Tyagaraja's contemporary.

47.s: Madhura Vijayam, also known as Veera Kamparaya Charitam, describes:
o: The conquest of Madurai by Kumara Kampana
The marriage of Achyuta Deva Raya and Varadambika
The legends of Rama in Telugu
The life of Venkateswara at Tirumala
47.x: Gangadevi's Sanskrit work Madhura Vijayam describes her husband Kumara Kampana's conquest of Madurai.
47.tq: Link the literary work to its historical subject rather than merely its author.
xs: **Madhura Vijayam** describes the **conquest of Madurai by Kumara Kampana** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was written in **Sanskrit** by **Gangadevi**, a **Sangama princess**, about her husband.
The marriage of Achyuta Deva Raya is **Varadambika Parinayam** (Oduva Tirumalamba).
xa: ⚠ PYQ (APPSC-G2 2023 and 2025): wrong match = **Gangadevi — Marichi Parinayam**.
**Molla Ramayanam** gives Rama's story in simple, elegant **Telugu**.

47.s: Tallapaka Timmakka wrote:
47.x: Timmakka wrote Subhadra Kalyanam; Molla wrote Molla Ramayanam and Vengamamba Venkatachala Mahatyamu.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** the **2025** answer key marked **Molla-Ramayanam** instead, but the explanation confirms Molla-Ramayanam is correct.
**Gangadevi** was a **Sangama princess**; husband **Kumara Kampana**.

47.s: Which of the following pairs (Telugu poet – title) is correctly matched?
47.x: Errapragada was Prabandha Parameswara; Nannaya was Adikavi and Tikkana was Kavibrahma.
xa: **Annamacharya** = **Padakavita Pitamaha**.
**China Tirumalacharya** = **Ashtabhasha Kavi Chakravarti**.

47.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Gatha Saptasati was authored by Hala.
Madhura Vijayam was authored by Gangadevi.
47.x: Option C is incorrect: Amuktamalyada was written by Krishnadevaraya; Tirumalamba wrote Varadambika Parinayam. Hala wrote Gatha Saptasati, Gangadevi Madhura Vijayam and Ketana Vignanesvaram.
47.tq: Match each work with its author.
n: Gatha Saptasati was written by Hala. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 9-11]
Vignanesvaram was written by Ketana. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 9-11]
Madhura Vijayam was written by Gangadevi. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 9-11]
Amuktamalyada was written by Krishnadevaraya. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 9-11]
xs: The incorrect statement: **Amuktamalyada** was authored by **Tirumalamba** — option **(3)**.
**Amuktamalyada** was written by **Krishnadevaraya**; **Allasani Peddana** was his court poet.
**Tirumalamba** wrote **Varadambika Parinayam**.
**Gangadevi** wrote **Madhura Vijayam** — option 2 is correct.
xa: Madhura Vijayam is in **Sanskrit**: Kumara Kampana's conquest of **Madurai**.
⚠ PYQ (APPSC-G2 **2023** and **2025**): wrong match = **Gangadevi - Marichi Parinayam**.
**Molla** = first Telugu woman poet to translate the Ramayana; **Timmakka** = first woman poet of the Andhra region.

47.s: Atukuri Molla, author of Molla Ramayanam, belonged to which community?
47.x: Molla came from the potter community and was the first Telugu woman to translate the Ramayana.

47.s: Amuktamalyada was written by:
47.x: Amuktamalyada is by Krishnadevaraya, not Tirumalamba; Allasani Peddana was his court poet.

47.s: Which pair (poet – title) is correctly matched?
47.x: Errapragada was Prabandha Parameswara; Nannaya was Adikavi, Tikkana Kavibrahma and Peddana Andhra Kavita Pitamaha.

47.s: Who established Saraswati Gachchas to promote education among common people?
47.x: The Jains established Saraswati Gachchas to spread education among common people.

47.s: The poets associated with the Bhakti tradition in Telugu contributed to Carnatic music chiefly through:
o: Only Persian ghazals and court chronicles
Padams, keertanas, satakas and dvipada compositions
Only Sanskrit inscriptions and copper plates
47.x: Telugu Bhakti poets carried devotional expression through padams, keertanas, satakas and dvipada compositions, helping establish the Telugu base of the Carnatic music repertoire.
47.tq: Identify the common cultural contribution across different literary forms.
xs: Telugu Bhakti was carried through **padams, keertanas, satakas and dvipada** compositions — option **(3)** is correct.
These became the **base of Carnatic music's Telugu repertoire**; Persian ghazals, military ballads and Sanskrit inscriptions are not the channel.
xa: **Annamacharya** = **Father of the Telugu keertana**; about **32,000 sankirtanas** to **Lord Venkateswara**.
**Kshetrayya** composed over a thousand **Movva Gopala padams** at **Abdullah Qutb Shah's** court.
**Tyagaraja** composed Telugu kritis and the **Pancharatna kritis** at **Tiruvaiyaru**; Carnatic Trinity with **Dikshitar** and **Syama Sastri**.
**Bhakta Ramadasu** composed the **Ramadasu kirtanas** and **Dasarathi Satakam**.

47.s:
Assertion (A): The Bhakti traditions did not uniformly uphold Brahmanical dominance.
Reason (R): Alvars, Nayanars and Basava, and in Andhra Vemana and Potuluri Veerabrahmam, criticised caste distinctions.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
47.x: These saints criticised caste and some promoted common dining of all castes, so the traditions challenged rather than upheld Brahmanical dominance.
xa: **Women saints**: **Andal**, **Karaikkal Ammaiyar**, **Akka Mahadevi**, **Atukuri Molla**.
Spread factors: **Chola patronage** and the **"little-great tradition"** fusion (Jagannath at Puri).

47.s: Which literary forms helped spread Bhakti ideas among common people in Andhra?
47.x: The satakam and dwipada forms helped communicate Bhakti ideas to common people in Telugu-speaking regions.
47.tq: Identify the regional literary forms associated with popular religious communication.
xs: The **Satakam and dwipada** forms spread bhakti to common people — option **(2)** is correct.
**Vachanas** are Kannada prose-poems and **Tevaram** is the Tamil Shaiva canon — not Andhra's forms.
xa: **Desi kavita**: simple native metres (**dwipada, ragada, manjari, kanda**) vs the Sanskritised **Marga** style.
**Palkuriki Somanatha** wrote **Basava Puranam** in simple Telugu **Dwipada** metre.

47.s:
Consider the following statements about the spread of Bhakti among common people:
1. Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam replaced Sanskrit as its vehicles.
2. Persian and Arabic were its main vehicles in South India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
47.x: Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam carried Bhakti ideas to common people instead of Sanskrit; Persian and Arabic were not its vehicles.

47.s: Akka Mahadevi, a woman saint of the Vachana tradition, belonged to:
47.x: Akka Mahadevi was a 12th-century Karnataka woman saint of the Vachana tradition.

47.s: Identify the wrong match. (Author) (Literary Work)
47.x: Gangadevi, the Vijayanagara-era Sanskrit poetess, wrote ' Madhura Vijayam ' celebrating her husband Kampana's conquest of Madurai-not ' Marichi Parinayam '. Molla's Telugu Ramayanam, Tallapaka Timmakka's ' Subhadra Kalyanam ' and Oduva Tirumalamba's ' Varadambika Parinayam ' are correctly matched. The question tests author-work pairing among medieval women writers.

48.s: Which of the following order of Sufism was against music :
48.x: Naqshbandi order was founded by Bahauddin Naqshband during the 14th century. Khwaja Khawand was the important saint of this order who came to India and made Kashmir as the centre of his activities. The promotion of this sect was mainly started around the (1563-1603) A.D., who came to Kabul on orders of his master. Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi also known as Mujaddid (the reformer of Islam) was his disciple. He propounded Wahdat-ul-Shuhud (positivist philosophy) which was against the order Sama (Music). It was the most radical order among Sufis. He also opposed liberal policies of Akbar. Aurangzeb was also influenced by this Sufiorder.

48.s: Which of the following is not related to Sufism?
48.x: ‘Khanqah’ was the place of residence of Sufi saints. ‘Sama’ was a function organised by Sufis. ‘Shaikh’ was the authorized person who provided education and guidance in Sufism. Ulemas were scholarly persons to know the religious laws of Islam. Therefore, Ulema is not related to Sufism.

48.s: Sufism absorbed ideas from Vedanta, Yoga and:
48.x: Sufism absorbed Vedanta, Yoga and Neo-Platonism while accepting the Quran and the Prophet.
xa: Sufis freely used **music**, which orthodox Islam did not generally sanction.
**Ba-shara** orders followed Sharia; **Be-shara** ones (wandering **Qalandars**, Madaris) were not bound by it.
Origin of 'Sufi': **Suf** (coarse wool), **Safa** (purity) or Greek **Sophia**.

48.s: Which of the following best expresses the social and cultural significance of Sufism in India?
o: It restricted religious interaction to Persian-speaking court elites.
It eliminated the use of local languages and music in religious life.
It functioned exclusively as a military organisation.
It gave Islam a tolerant, vernacular face and made khanqahs welfare centres.
48.x: Sufism gave Islam in India a tolerant and vernacular character, while khanqahs served as welfare centres.
48.tq: Apply the broader social significance to a description.
xs: Sufism gave Islam in India a **tolerant, vernacular face**, and **khanqahs served as welfare centres** — option **(4)** is correct.
It did the opposite of options (1) and (2): Chishtis adapted to **local language and music**.
xa: Chishti adaptation made Sufism the **bridge for Indo-Islamic composite culture**.
Khanqahs gave **food and shelter to the poor**.

48.s: One derivation of 'Sufi' is from 'suf', meaning:
48.x: Suf means coarse wool; the word is also explained through safa (purity) and the Greek sophia.
xa: First prominent Sufi in India: **Ali Hujwiri (Data Ganj Bakhsh)**, author of **Kashf-ul-Mahjub**.
Most popular order in India: **Chishti**.
Sufis accepted the **Quran and the Prophet** but absorbed **Vedanta, Yoga, Neo-Platonism**.

48.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ali Hujwiri — first prominent Sufi in India; Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Dehlavi — last great Chishti of Delhi
Moinuddin Chishti — first prominent Sufi in India; Salim Chishti — last great Chishti of Delhi
Ahmad Sirhindi — first prominent Sufi in India; Baba Farid — last great Chishti of Delhi
Burhanuddin Gharib — first prominent Sufi in India; Gesudaraz — last great Chishti of Delhi
48.x: Ali Hujwiri is identified as the first prominent Sufi in India, while Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Dehlavi is the last great Chishti saint of Delhi.
48.tq: Use the first/last clues to split the options.
xs: **Ali Hujwiri** = first prominent Sufi in India; **Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Dehlavi** = last great Chishti of Delhi — option **(1)** is correct.
**Moinuddin Chishti** founded the Chishti order in India; **Salim Chishti** was **Akbar's** saint.
**Burhanuddin Gharib** and **Gesudaraz** belong to the **Deccan**, not Delhi.
xa: Ali Hujwiri wrote **Kashf-ul-Mahjub**; title **Data Ganj Bakhsh**.
Nasiruddin = **Chiragh-i-Delhi** (UPPSC 2017, UKPSC 2025).
48.fixed: drop odd phrase 'in the specified Sufi context'

48.s: The Ulema were:
48.x: The Ulema were scholars of Islamic law, not Sufis, and generally did not sanction music.

48.s: Who was the last great Chishti saint of Delhi?
48.x: Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Dehlavi was the last great Chishti of Delhi.

48.s: Which Christian saint is famous for the love of animals and birds?
48.x: Saint Francis of Assisi (1181 or 82-1226 A.D.) is famous for his love of birds and animals.

48.s: From the given pairs identify the incorrect pair –
48.x: The dominion of Chishti order existed in Delhi and surrounding areas while the area of Suhrawardi order existed in Sindh region. Firdausi order was a part of Chishti order whose dominion existed in the region of Bihar. Auliya is not any order, but a title given to ‘Nizamuddin’ the famous Saint of Delhi. The dominion of Nizamuddin Auliya existed in Delhi. Thus, option (c) is incorrect.

48.s: ‘SufiKalam,’ a type of devotional music, is characteristic of:
48.x: ‘SufiKalam’ a type of devotional music is characteristic of Jammu and Kashmir.

48.s: A khanqah in the Sufi tradition was primarily a place that
o: served as a hospice where disciples lived and trained, while also providing food and shelter to the poor
was a military camp maintained by Sufi rulers
functioned exclusively as a court for settling criminal disputes
served only as a shrine over a saint’s tomb
48.x: A khanqah was a Sufi hospice for the residence and training of disciples, and it also provided food and shelter to the poor.
48.tq: Identify the institution from its combined training and charitable functions.
xs: A **khanqah** was a **Sufi hospice** where disciples lived and trained, also giving **food and shelter to the poor** — option **(1)** is correct.
A shrine at a saint's tomb is a **Dargah**, not a khanqah.
xa: At **Golconda**, khanqahs served as **higher-education centres**.
Khanqahs served as **welfare centres**, giving Islam in India a tolerant face.
**Nizamuddin Auliya's** hospice drew both **common people and nobles**.

48.s: Sama in Sufi practice refers to
o: the spiritual path leading through the maqamat
devotional music intended to produce ecstasy
the death anniversary of a saint
48.x: Sama means devotional music intended to produce spiritual ecstasy. Raqs refers to the ritual dance associated with it.
48.tq: Distinguish closely related Sufi technical terms by their precise meanings.
xs: **Sama** is **devotional music meant to produce ecstasy** — option **(2)** is correct.
The spiritual path is **Tariqa**; repetition of God's name is **Zikr**; a saint's death anniversary is **Urs**.
xa: **Raqs** = ritual dance; **'Majlis-i-Sama'** of **Chishtis and Suhrawardis**.
⚠ **Chishtis encouraged** sama and qawwali; **Naqshbandis opposed** sama.
**Amir Khusrau** introduced **Qaul**, the opening hymn of Qawwali.

48.s: The bond between a spiritual master and his disciple in Sufism is known as
48.x: The pir–murid relationship is called Piri-Muridi. The pir or murshid is the spiritual master and the murid is the disciple.
48.tq: Test the exact term for a relationship rather than for an individual role.
xs: The pir-murid bond (preceptorship) is called **Piri-Muridi** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Wahdat-ush-Shuhud** is Sirhindi's doctrine; **Fana-Baqa** is annihilation / subsistence in God; **Ba-shara** means following the Shariat.
xa: **Pir / Murshid** = spiritual master or guide.
**Murid** = disciple pledged in **absolute submission** to the pir.

48.s: Fana and Baqa respectively signify
o: remembrance of God and ritual dance
annihilation of the self in God and subsistence in God
48.x: Fana denotes annihilation of the self or ego in God, while Baqa denotes subsistence in God.
48.tq: Test the paired terms together to prevent reversal of their meanings.
xs: **Fana** = **annihilation of the self in God**; **Baqa** = **subsistence in God** — option **(4)** is correct.
Remembrance of God = **Zikr**; ritual dance = **Raqs**; guide and disciple = **Pir and Murid**.
xa: **Kashf-ul-Mahjub** of Ali Hujwiri treats **fana** as a theme.
The **10 maqamat** run from **Tauba** (repentance) to **Riza** (submission).

48.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
48.x: Tazkiras are biographies of saints. Anti-Shia tracts are represented by works such as ‘Radd-i-Khawafiq’.
48.tq: Find the incorrectly defined paired term.
xs: **Tazkiras — anti-Shia tracts** is wrong — option **(1)** is the answer; tazkiras are **biographies of saints**.
Anti-Shia tracts: e.g. Sirhindi's **Radd-i-Khawafiq**.
**Malfuzat = recorded conversations**; **Maktubat = letters** are correct.
xa: **Siyar-ul-Auliya** of **Mir Khwurd Kirmani** is a tazkira.
**Maktubat-i-Imam Rabbani** = letters of **Ahmad Sirhindi**.

48.s: In Sufism, 'Urs' refers to:
o: a saint's death anniversary, seen as union with God
a friend of God or saint
a shrine at a saint's tomb
48.x: Urs is a saint's death anniversary viewed as union with God; dargah is the shrine, wali the saint and tariqa the path.
xa: The **ulema** stood for **legalistic orthodoxy and the Shariat**.
**Chilla** = solitude or retreat; **Zikr** = continuous remembrance of God's name.

48.s: In Sufi literature, 'Malfuzat' are:
48.x: Malfuzat are conversations; Maktubat are letters and Tazkiras biographies.

48.s: In Sufism, 'Wali' or 'Auliya' means:
48.x: Wali/Auliya means friend(s) of God, a saint; Auliya is a title, not an order.

48.s: The doctrine of Wahdat-ul-Wujud is associated with:
48.x: Wahdat-ul-Wujud was associated with Ibn Arabi; Sirhindi represented Wahdat-ush-Shuhud.
xa: Wujud = **Unity of Being** (Haq and Khalq are one); Shuhud = **Unity of Appearance/Witness**.
The **Qadiri** order **backed Wahdat-ul-Wujud**.

48.s: In the Sufi scheme of ten stages (maqamat), the first and the last stages are respectively
48.x: The ten maqamat begin with Tauba (repentance) and end with Riza (submission), passing through Wara, Zuhd, Faqr, Sabr, Shukr, Khauf, Raja and Tawakkul. Zuhd, Faqr, Sabr and Shukr are intermediate stages, and 'Riza and Tauba' reverses the order.
xs: The maqamat begin with **Tauba** (repentance) and end with **Riza** (submission) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Zuhd, Faqr, Sabr, Shukr** are intermediate stages; option (4) reverses the order.
xa: The **10 stages**: Tauba → **Wara, Zuhd, Faqr, Sabr, Shukr, Khauf, Raja, Tawakkul** → Riza.
**Tariqa** = spiritual path through stages.

48.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Wahdat-ul-Wujud — Unity of Being; Haq and Khalq are one
Wahdat-ush-Shuhud — Creator and creation are identical
Wahdat-ush-Shuhud — Doctrine associated with Ibn Arabi
48.x: Wahdat-ul-Wujud means Unity of Being and identifies Haq, the Creator, with Khalq, creation. Wahdat-ush-Shuhud means Unity of Appearance or Witness and holds that creation reflects God rather than being identical with Him.
48.tq: Distinguish the two doctrines by comparing identity with reflection.
xs: **Wahdat-ul-Wujud** = **"Unity of Being"**: **Haq** (Creator) and **Khalq** (creation) are one — option **(1)** is correct.
**Wahdat-ush-Shuhud** = **"Unity of Appearance/Witness"**: creation **only reflects God** — so options (2) and (3) swap the meanings.
Wahdat-ush-Shuhud belongs to **Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi**, not **Ibn Arabi**.
xa: ⚠ **Wujud** = Being (Ibn Arabi, **Qadiri**, **Chishti**); **Shuhud** = Appearance (Sirhindi, **Naqshbandi**).
Sirhindi, the **Naqshbandi** saint, framed Wahdat-ush-Shuhud as his **counter-doctrine**.

48.s: The doctrine of Wahdat-ush-Shuhud is associated with:
48.x: Wahdat-ush-Shuhud (Unity of Appearance) was taught by Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi; Wahdat-ul-Wujud is Ibn Arabi's.

48.s: Wahdat-ul-Wujud holds that:
48.x: Wahdat-ul-Wujud (Unity of Being) holds that Haq and Khalq are one; the view that creation only reflects God is Wahdat-ush-Shuhud.

48.s: Who wrote the book Tehgig-a-Hind?
Alberuni noted similarities between Sufi ideas and the Gita and:
48.x: Alberuni compared Sufi ideas with Patanjali's Yoga Sutra and the Gita.
xa: Sufis also met the **Kanphata (Nath) yogis** of **Gorakhnath**.
Sufism absorbed **Vedanta**, **Yoga** and **Neo-Platonism**.

48.s: Breath control became vital in almost every Sufi order after the translation of:
48.x: Breath control spread after the translation of Amritakund, the Naqshbandis being the exception.
xa: Amritakund was translated into **Arabic and Persian** in the **13th c.**
**Shattaris** were liberal and **absorbed yogic practices**.

48.s: The Hatha-yogic text translated into Arabic and Persian in the 13th century was:
48.x: Amritakund was translated in the 13th century; after it breath control became key in most Sufi orders.

48.s: Breath control became vital in almost every Sufi order EXCEPT the:
48.x: After the Amritakund translation, breath control spread to nearly every order except the Naqshbandis.

48.s: In Sufi practice, 'chilla' refers to:
48.x: Chilla is solitude or retreat; zikr is remembrance of God and raqs the ritual dance.

48.s: Which of the following was a Be-shara group?
48.x: The Madaris and wandering Qalandars were Be-shara; the Naqshbandi and Firdausi were Ba-shara orders.
xa: Other Ba-shara orders: **Chishti**, **Suhrawardi**, **Qadiri**.
Ba-shara = follow the **Shariat**; Be-shara = **outside it**.

48.s: The term 'Be-shara' refers to Sufis who:
48.x: Be-shara Sufis, like the wandering Qalandars, lived outside the Sharia; Ba-shara orders followed it.

48.s: The Sufi saint who maintained that devotional music was one way of coming close to God was
48.x: The Chishti order accepted sama (devotional music) as a legitimate means of experiencing closeness to God. Muinud-din Chishti played a key role in popularising this tradition in India through the Chishti movement centred at Ajmer.

48.s:
Assertion (A): The sponsor and the most prominent figure of the Chisti order of Sufis in India is Khwaja Moinuddin Chisti.
Reason (R): The Chisti order takes its name from a village, Chisti, in Ajmer. In the context of the above two statements, which one of the following is correct?
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
48.x: Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti was indeed the most prominent figure of the Chishti order in India and established it at Ajmer. However, the order takes its name from Chisht, a town in present-day Afghanistan — not from Ajmer.

48.s: In June, 2012 a fierce fire damaged the sacred site of Dastagir Sahib in Srinagar. Who among the following is known as Dastgir Sahib?
48.x: Dastgir Sahib is related to Abdul Qadir Jilani, the patron of the Qadiri Silsila. Hence, Abdul Qadir Jilani is known as Dastagir Sahib. It is a sacred Sufi place which is 200 years old. Here, old 'Quran' written by Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiqi, Hazrat Ali & Mou-i Pak & piece of Hair from Ghaus-e-Azam has been kept. The site was damaged by fire in June, 2012, but important remains were preserved due to fire extinguishers.

48.s: Which of the following Sufis regarded Krishna among the Auliyas :
48.x: The Sufi saint Shah Muhammad Ghaus accepted Lord Krishna as Auliya/Wali. He was the most famous saint of Shattari order. He had a close relationship with Mughal emperor Humayun and Tansen. He expressed his spiritual quest in ‘Jawahir-e-Khamsa’. He translated ‘Amritkund’ of Hatha yoga by the name of ‘Bahar-ul-Hayat.’ Shattari Saints tried to bring about reconciliation between Muslims and Hindus by showing equality in religious ideas and practices.

48.s:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as
Assertion (A) and the other labelled as
Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : The sponsor and the most prominent figure of the Chishti order of Sufis in India is Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti.
Reason (R) : The Chishti order takes its name from a village Chishti in Ajmer. In the context of the above two statements, which one of the following is correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) is individually true, and (R) is the
Both (A) and (R) is individually true, but (R) is not
48.x: The Chishti order was founded by Khwaja Abu Ishaq Shami of Syria, but it was introduced in India by Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti, who came along with Muhammad Ghori army in 1192 AD. Khwaja Abu Ishaq Sami migrated from Syria to Chist (Chishti Sharif, Afghanistan), hence, was called Chishti. He was 9th generation descendant of Hazrat Ali. Therefore, assertion (A) is right, but reason (R) is wrong.

48.s: The “Chishtia SufiOrder” in India was established by-
48.x: The “Chishtia SufiOrder” was established in Chishti Sharif of Afghanistan by Abu Ishaq Shami Chishti and his disciple Khwaja Abu Ahmad Abdal, but it was primarily established in India by Muinuddin Chishti. He came to India with the army of Muhammad Ghori in 1192 A.D. (12th century) and made Ajmer, Rajasthan his abode. He died in 1236 AD. Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki was his disciple.

48.s: The Sufisaint who maintained that devotional music was one way of coming close to God was :
48.x: Muinuddin Chishti introduced the Chishti order of Sufism in India. He maintained that devotional music was one way to come closer to God.

48.s: The most orthodox Sufiorder was –
48.x: Baha-ud-Din Naqshband founded the SufiNaqshbandi order in 14th century. This order was made popular in India by Babur. Insistence on rigid adherence to Shariat and nurturing love for Prophet was the essence of this order. According to Jharkhand Public Service Commission, option (b) is the correct answer.

48.s: The spread of which of the following Sufisect was mostly limited to Sindh, Multan and Punjab?
48.x: The Suhrawardi SufiSect entered India at about the same time as Chishtis sect but its activities were confined largely to the Punjab, Multan and Sindh. This SufiSect was established in India by Baha-Ud-Din Zakariya.

48.s: Who among the following does not belong to the Chishti order?
48.x: Chishti order is a Sunni Sufiorder within the mystic Sufitradition of Islam. Muinuddin Chishti introduced the Chishti order in India. Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki was a saint of Chishti order from Delhi; Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya was a saint of Chishti order in Indian sub-continent. Shaikh Abdul Jilani did not belong to Chishti Silsila. Rather, he founded Qadiri order.

48.s: Who among the following Chishti Saints is known as 'Chirag-i-Delhi?
48.x: Shaikh Nasiruddin Mahmud was a disciple of Sufi saint Nizamuddin Auliya. He was given the title of 'Chirag-i-Dehlavi'.

48.s: Which Sufi order was strictly orthodox and opposed Akbar's Sulh-i-Kul?
48.x: The Naqshbandis opposed Sulh-i-Kul; the Chishtis kept aloof from the court, the Suhrawardis accepted royal service and the Shattaris absorbed yogic practices.
xa: ⚠ Chishti (aloof, sama) vs Suhrawardi (close to court) = **most-asked contrast**; Naqshbandi = the **orthodox pole**.
Naqshbandis also opposed **Shia influence**.

48.s: The Naqshbandi order originated in Central Asia with:
48.x: The order began with Bahauddin Naqshband; in India it was associated with Khwaja Baqi Billah and Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi.
xa: Naqshbandis were the **most orthodox** (JPSC 2016); **opposed sama** and visits to saints' tombs.
Sirhindi was **imprisoned by Jahangir**.

48.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Muhammad Ghaus of Gwalior — Shattari order
48.x: Abdul Qadir Jilani founded the Qadiri order; he was not a Chishti saint. Shah Abdullah Shattari, Muhammad Ghaus and Sharafuddin Yahya Maneri are correctly associated with the orders shown.
48.tq: The wrong-founder trap distinguishes Abdul Qadir Jilani from the Chishti order.
xs: **Abdul Qadir Jilani — Chishti** is wrong — option **(1)** is the answer; he **founded the Qadiri order** (RPSC 2016).
**Shah Abdullah Shattari** founded the **Shattari** order; **Muhammad Ghaus of Gwalior** was Shattari.
**Sharafuddin Yahya Maneri** belongs to the **Firdausi** order of **Bihar**.
xa: Chishti founder at Chisht (Herat): **Khwaja Abu Ishaq Shami**; in India **Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti**.
**Mahdawi** order = **Syed Muhammad of Jaunpur**.

48.s: Regarding the Naqshbandi order, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Bahauddin Zakariya established its main khanqah at Multan.
Bahauddin Naqshband himself established the order in India during Akbar's reign.
Moinuddin Chishti brought the order to India with Muhammad Ghori.
Khwaja Baqi Billah brought the order to India in the late sixteenth century.
48.x: Bahauddin Naqshband was the Central Asian founder and was revered by Babur, but he did not come to India. Khwaja Baqi Billah brought the Naqshbandi order to India in the late sixteenth century.
48.tq: Separate the original founder outside India from the person who introduced the order in India.
xs: **Khwaja Baqi Billah** brought the Naqshbandi order to India in the **late 16th c.** — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ **Bahauddin Naqshband** founded it in Central Asia but **never came to India**.
**Bahauddin Zakariya** (Multan) was **Suhrawardi**; **Moinuddin Chishti** came with **Muhammad Ghori** as the **Chishti** founder.
xa: The order was revered by **Babur**.
Indian Naqshbandis: **Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi**, **Shah Waliullah**, **Shah Abdul Aziz**.

48.s: Which comparison between the Chishti and Suhrawardi orders is correct?
o: Chishtis were close to the court, whereas Suhrawardis rejected sama entirely.
Chishtis were the orthodox pole, whereas Suhrawardis were wandering Qalandars.
Chishtis were generally aloof and associated with sama, whereas Suhrawardis maintained closeness to the court.
Both orders were Be-shara and rejected Islamic law.
48.x: The Chishtis are contrasted with the Suhrawardis as relatively aloof and associated with sama, while the Suhrawardis were closer to the court.
48.tq: Use the central contrast rather than a shared feature.
xs: **Chishtis** were **aloof and associated with sama**; **Suhrawardis** stayed **close to the court** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **orthodox pole** was the **Naqshbandi**, not the Chishti; **Qalandars** were Be-shara wanderers.
Both Chishti and Suhrawardi were **Ba-shara**, following Sharia.
xa: ⚠ This Chishti vs Suhrawardi contrast is the **most-asked** one.
Bahauddin Zakariya (Suhrawardi) got the title **Shaikh-ul-Islam** from Iltutmish.

48.s: The Firdausi order, led by Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri, flourished in:
48.x: The Firdausis followed Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri in Bihar; the Suhrawardis followed Bahauddin Zakariya in Multan and Sindh.
n: The Suhrawardi Sufi Silsilah is associated with Bahauddin Zakariya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Suhrawardi Sufi Silsilah is associated with Multan. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Suhrawardi Sufi Silsilah is associated with Punjab. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Suhrawardi Sufi Silsilah is associated with Sindh. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Firdausia Sufi Silsilah is associated with Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Firdausia Sufi Silsilah is associated with Bihar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Naqshbandi Sufi Silsilah opposed Sama. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Naqshbandi Sufi Silsilah emphasized Shariat. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Ahmad Sirhindi was associated with the Naqshbandi Sufi Silsilah. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Qadiri Sufi Silsilah followed the tradition of Abdul Qadir Jilani. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
xa: **Chishti** — **Muinuddin Chishti**, **Ajmer**.
Bahauddin Zakariya backed **Iltutmish against Qabacha** and got the title **Shaikh-ul-Islam**.
⚠ **Wahdat-ul-Wujud** = Qadiri/Chishti; **Wahdat-ush-Shuhud** = Sirhindi (Naqshbandi).

48.s: Who established the Chishti Sufi silsilah in India?
48.x: Muinuddin Chishti brought the Chishti silsilah to India and set it up at Ajmer. Shahabuddin Suhrawardi is linked to the Suhrawardi order, Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri to the Firdausi order and Bahauddin Naqshband to the Naqshbandi order.
48.tq: Link each silsilah to its founder.
n: Muinuddin Chishti is associated with the Chishti Sufi silsilah. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 134-135]
Shahabuddin Suhrawardi is associated with the Suhrawardi Sufi silsilah. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 134-135]
Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri is associated with the Firdausi Sufi silsilah. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 134-135]
Bahauddin Naqshband is associated with the Naqshbandi Sufi silsilah. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 134-135]
xs: **Muinuddin Chishti** established the Chishti silsilah in India — option **(4)**.
He settled at **Ajmer**, having come with **Muhammad Ghori** in **1192**.
**Shahabuddin Suhrawardi** founded the **Suhrawardi**; **Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri** — **Firdausi**; **Bahauddin Naqshband** — **Naqshbandi**.
xa: ⚠ Sources differ: the order was founded at **Chisht** (Herat) by **Khwaja Abu Ishaq Shami**.
The Chishtis **kept aloof** from court and encouraged **sama** and qawwali.
Chishti = **most popular order** in India.

48.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of saints belonging to the Chishti Silsila?
o: Miyan Mir, Muhibullah Shah, Dara Shikoh and Burhanuddin Gharib
Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Dehlavi, Burhanuddin Gharib, Gesudaraz and Hamiduddin of Nagaur
Khwaja Baqi Billah, Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi, Shah Waliullah and Hamiduddin Nagori
Bahauddin Zakariya, Ruknuddin Abul Fath, Jalaluddin Tabrizi and Gesudaraz
48.x: Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Dehlavi, Burhanuddin Gharib, Gesudaraz and the Chishti Hamiduddin of Nagaur are all associated with the Chishti order.

xs: **Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Dehlavi, Burhanuddin Gharib, Gesudaraz and Hamiduddin of Nagaur** are all Chishtis — option **(2)** is correct.
**Miyan Mir, Muhibullah Shah, Dara Shikoh** = **Qadiri**; **Baqi Billah, Sirhindi, Shah Waliullah** = **Naqshbandi**.
**Bahauddin Zakariya, Ruknuddin Abul Fath, Jalaluddin Tabrizi** = **Suhrawardi**.

Other Chishtis: **Moinuddin**, **Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki**, **Baba Farid**, **Nizamuddin Auliya**.

48.s: Qazi Hamiduddin Nagori belonged to which Sufi order?
48.x: Qazi Hamiduddin Nagori was a Suhrawardi, unlike the Chishti Hamiduddin of Nagaur, a disciple of Moinuddin Chishti.
xa: ⚠ Some notes list "Hamiduddin Nagori" under the Suhrawardis — keep the two apart.
Moinuddin Chishti (**1143-1235**) has his dargah at **Ajmer**.

48.s: Abul Hasan Tana Shah, the last Qutb Shahi ruler of Golconda, was a disciple of which saint?
48.x: Abul Hasan Tana Shah was a disciple of the Chishti saint Shah Raju Qattal.

xs: **Abul Hasan Tana Shah**, last Qutb Shahi, was a disciple of the Chishti saint **Shah Raju Qattal** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Sirhindi** was Naqshbandi; **Bahauddin Zakariya** was Suhrawardi of Multan; **Bakhtiyar Kaki** was a Delhi Chishti.

Golconda khanqahs = **higher-education centres**.

48.s: Abdul Qadir Jilani founded which Sufi order?
48.x: Abdul Qadir Jilani of Baghdad founded the Qadiri order; he was not a Chishti.

48.s: Dara Shikoh and Miyan Mir belonged to which Sufi order?
48.x: Miyan Mir, Muhibullah Shah and Dara Shikoh were Qadiris.

48.s: Shah Muhammad Ghaus of Gwalior belonged to which order?
48.x: Shah Muhammad Ghaus was a Shattari saint, close to Humayun and Tansen; he wrote Jawahir-e-Khamsa.

48.s: The Chishti order takes its name from Chisht, which is in:
48.x: Chisht is a town in Afghanistan, not a village in Ajmer.

48.x: Moinuddin Chishti came with Muhammad Ghori's army in 1192 and settled at Ajmer.

48.x: Early Chishtis avoided court patronage and state grants, while later Deccan Chishtis accepted grants; they encouraged sama and qawwali.

48.s: Bahauddin Zakariya was given which title after supporting Iltutmish against Qabacha?
48.x: Bahauddin Zakariya received the title Shaikh-ul-Islam after backing Iltutmish against Qabacha.

xs: **Bahauddin Zakariya** backed **Iltutmish against Qabacha** and got the title **Shaikh-ul-Islam** — option **(3)** is correct.
He was the **Suhrawardi** saint of **Multan**; the order stayed close to rulers.
xa: ⚠ Chishti = aloof + sama; Suhrawardi = court + **Shaikh-ul-Islam**; Naqshbandi = most orthodox.
Suhrawardis accepted **wealth and posts**.

48.s: Which Sufi order opposed sama?
48.x: The Naqshbandis opposed sama, while the Chishtis encouraged sama and qawwali and the Suhrawardis adopted sama and raqs.

Naqshbandis also opposed **visits to saints' tombs**.

48.s: Ahmad Sirhindi criticised Akbar’s Sulh-i-Kul and was subsequently imprisoned by which Mughal ruler?
48.x: Ahmad Sirhindi criticised Akbar’s Sulh-i-Kul and was imprisoned during the reign of Jahangir.
48.tq: Separate the ruler whose policy was criticised from the ruler who ordered the imprisonment.
xs: **Ahmad Sirhindi** criticised Akbar's **Sulh-i-Kul** and was **imprisoned by Jahangir** — option **(2)** is correct.
As a strictly orthodox **Naqshbandi**, he opposed Sulh-i-Kul and **Shia influence**.
xa: Sirhindi's title: **Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani**.
He propounded **Wahdat-ush-Shuhud** against Wahdat-ul-Wujud.

48.s: Ahmad Sirhindi was known by which title?
48.x: Ahmad Sirhindi of the Naqshbandi order was called Mujaddid Alif Sani, the reviver of the second Islamic millennium. Chirag-i-Delhi was Nasiruddin Mahmud and Mehboob-i-Ilahi was Nizamuddin Auliya.
48.tq: Link each title to its saint.
n: Nizamuddin Auliya was known as Mehboob-i-Ilahi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Nasiruddin Mahmud was known as Chirag-i-Delhi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Salim Chishti was known as Shaikh-ul-Hind. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Ahmad Sirhindi was known as Mujaddid Alif Sani. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Ahmad Sirhindi is associated with Wahdat-ul-Shuhud. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
xs: Ahmad Sirhindi was called **Mujaddid Alif Sani** — option **(4)**.

**Chirag-i-Delhi** = **Nasiruddin Mahmud**; **Mehboob-i-Ilahi** = **Nizamuddin Auliya**; **Shaikh-ul-Hind** = **Salim Chishti**.

He propounded **Wahdat-ush-Shuhud** ("Unity of Appearance").
His letters: **Maktubat-i-Imam Rabbani**; anti-Shia tract: **Radd-i-Khawafiq**.

48.s: The Mausoleum (Dargah) of which Chishti Saint was visited by Akbar ?

48.s: The dargah of Gesudaraz is at:

**Nizamuddin Auliya** and **Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Dehlavi** — **Delhi**.

48.x: Nasiruddin Mahmud was Chirag-i-Delhi; Nizamuddin Auliya was Mehboob-i-Ilahi and Salim Chishti Shaikh-ul-Hind.

Salim Chishti was known as Shaikh-ul-Hind. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]

48.s: Amir Khusrau, the disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya, introduced which element of Qawwali?
o: Fana, the final stage of spiritual union
48.x: Amir Khusrau introduced Qaul, the opening hymn of Qawwali.
48.tq: Associate a cultural contribution with its contributor.
xs: **Amir Khusrau** introduced **Qaul**, the opening hymn of Qawwali — option **(1)** is correct.
**Malfuzat** are recorded conversations; **Fana** is annihilation of self in God; **Khanqah** is a hospice — none is a Qawwali element.
xa: Khusrau was a disciple of **Nizamuddin Auliya**.
The **Chishtis encouraged sama and qawwali**; the Naqshbandis opposed sama.

48.s: Kashf-ul-Mahjub was written by:

⚠ FIRST = **Ali Hujwiri**; last great Chishti of Delhi = **Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Dehlavi**.

48.s: The dargah of Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki is at:
48.x: Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki, disciple of Moinuddin, is buried at Mehrauli in Delhi.

48.s: The dargah of Salim Chishti is at:
48.x: Salim Chishti (Shaikh-ul-Hind) is buried at Fatehpur Sikri.

48.x: Baba Farid's disciples were Nizamuddin Auliya and Alauddin Sabir (Kaliyari).

48.s: Hamiduddin of Nagaur, a disciple of Moinuddin Chishti, belonged to which order?
48.x: Hamiduddin of Nagaur was a Chishti; Qazi Hamiduddin Nagori was a Suhrawardi.

48.s:

48.x: Baba Farid was Ganj-i-Shakar and Moinuddin's dargah is at Ajmer; Nizamuddin lived at Ajodhan and Delhi, not Multan.

48.s: ‘Maktubat-i-Imam Rabbani’ is best described as which of the following?
o: An anti-Shia tract by Abdul Haqq Dehlavi
A tazkira written by Mir Khwurd Kirmani

The anti-Shia tract is Sirhindi's **Radd-i-Khawafiq**; the tazkira by **Mir Khwurd Kirmani** is **Siyar-ul-Auliya**.

Sirhindi = **Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani**, a **Naqshbandi**.

48.s: Fawaid-ul-Fuad, the malfuzat of Nizamuddin Auliya, was compiled by:
48.x: Amir Hasan Sijzi compiled Fawaid-ul-Fuad; Mir Khwurd Kirmani wrote Siyar-ul-Auliya.

48.s: Radd-i-Khawafiq, an anti-Shia tract, was written by:
48.x: Radd-i-Khawafiq is Ahmad Sirhindi's anti-Shia tract.

48.s: Siyar-ul-Auliya, a tazkira of Chishti saints, was written by:
48.x: Siyar-ul-Auliya is a tazkira by Mir Khwurd Kirmani.

48.s: The Baba Fakhruddin Dargah is located at:

Ameen Peer Dargah = **Peerullah Hussaini**, **17th c.**

48.s: The dargah of Gesudaraz, also known as Bande Nawaz, is located at which place?
48.x: The dargah of Gesudaraz or Bande Nawaz is at Gulbarga, where he settled under the Bahmanis.
xs: **Gesudaraz (Bande Nawaz)** has his dargah at **Gulbarga** (Kalaburagi) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Khuldabad** = **Burhanuddin Gharib**; **Bijapur** = later Chishti centre; **Golconda** = **Shah Raju Qattal**.
xa: He settled there under the **Bahmanis**.
⚠ **APPSC 2018:** **Gesudaraz** = the Chishti in the list.

48.s: Which of the following pairs (Sufi saint – place/title) is correctly matched?
48.x: Burhanuddin Gharib settled at Daulatabad; Nasiruddin Mahmud was Chirag-i-Delhi, Salim Chishti lived at Fatehpur Sikri and Gesu Daraz at Gulbarga.
n: Nasiruddin Mahmud belonged to the Chishti order. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Nasiruddin Mahmud was known as Chirag-i-Delhi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Salim Chishti belonged to the Chishti order. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Salim Chishti is associated with Fatehpur Sikri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Burhanuddin Gharib belonged to the Chishti order. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Burhanuddin Gharib is associated with Daulatabad. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Shaikh Mohammad Hussaini belonged to the Chishti order. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Shaikh Mohammad Hussaini is associated with Gulbarga. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
xa: ⚠ Sources differ: other notes place Burhanuddin Gharib at **Khuldabad**, in the **14th c.**
Gesudaraz (**Banda Nawaz**) has his dargah at **Gulbarga**.
Salim Chishti was called **Shaikh-ul-Hind**.

48.s: Who took the Chishti order to the Deccan, at Khuldabad, in the 14th century?

xa: **Gesudaraz (Bande Nawaz)** settled at **Gulbarga** under the **Bahmanis**.
**Bijapur** became a later key Chishti centre in the Deccan.

48.s: The Ameen Peer Dargah (Asthana-e-Magdoomiya) is located at:
48.x: The Ameen Peer Dargah of Peerullah Hussaini (17th c.) is at Kadapa; the Baba Fakhruddin Dargah is at Penukonda.

48.s: At which Kurnool district dargah is the Ugadi Panchanga Shravanam read jointly by a Sufi and a Brahmin priest?
48.x: At the Kowthalam dargah of Hazrath Shah Abdul Quadir, a Sufi and a Brahmin priest read the Ugadi Panchanga together.

48.s: Shaikh Bahauddin Zakaria belonged to which sect?
48.x: Shaikh Bahauddin Zakaria started Suhrawardi order in India. Shaikh Sadr-ud-din Arif, Shaikh Rakh-ud-din Abul Fateh and Shaikh Jalaluddin Surkh were associated with this Sufisect.

49.s: Which one of the following best explains the difference between Bhakti devotion and formal Sufi religious practice?
o: Bhakti rejected personal devotion, whereas Sufism confined worship to idol rituals.
Bhakti emphasised Vedic ritual, whereas Sufism rejected all forms of devotion.
Bhakti stressed devotion over Vedic ritual, while Sufism valued inner experience over formal Shariat.
Both movements exclusively supported priestly authority and formal ritual.
49.x: Bhakti traditions placed devotion above Vedic ritual and priestly mediation, while Sufism emphasised inner spiritual experience rather than merely formal observance of the Shariat.
49.tq: Test a comparison by matching each tradition with its characteristic emphasis.
xs: **Bhakti** put devotion over **Vedic ritual and priests**; **Sufism** put **inner experience over the formal Shariat** — option **(3)** is correct.
Neither movement backed priestly authority or idol rituals, so options (1), (2), (4) are wrong.
xa: The **guru / pir** bond was central to both.
Also shared: **vernacular preaching** and **spiritual equality of all castes**.

49.s: Which of the following was NOT shared by the Bhakti and Sufi traditions?
49.x: Both valued the guide-disciple bond, devotion over ritual and vernacular preaching; exclusive idol worship was not common to them.
xa: APPSC 2022 and 2023 keyed **monotheism, asceticism, tolerance** as common.
Both stressed **spiritual equality of all castes**.

49.s: Which of the following was NOT common to the Bhakti and Sufi movements?
49.x: Monotheism, asceticism and religious tolerance were common; idol worship was rejected by the Sufis and the Nirguna saints.
xa: Bhakti monotheism: **Nirguna saints**; Sufi: **Tawhid**, **Wahdat-ul-Wujud**.
Tolerance: Kabir and Nanak criticised **both Hindu and Muslim orthodoxy**.

49.s: Kabir and Nanak criticised the rigid orthodoxy of:
49.x: Kabir and Nanak criticised the orthodoxies of both Hinduism and Islam and stressed spiritual equality.
xa: Kabir's mission: **Hindu-Muslim unity**; God as Ram, Rahim, Allah, Khuda, Hari.
**Kabir, Nanak, Ravidas, Dadu** = **Kabirpanth + Sant (Nirguna) tradition**.

49.s: Which one of the following developments represents the later limitation of the Bhakti and Sufi movements?
o: The movements became confined only to royal courts.
Vernacular devotional traditions were entirely abandoned.
Their traditions hardened into separate sects and panths.
49.x: The movements later hardened into separate sects and panths, despite their earlier emphasis on broad spiritual and social interaction.
49.tq: Identify the later reversal of an initially inclusive tendency.
xs: The movements later **hardened into separate sects and panths** — option **(4)** is correct.
They did not abandon vernaculars or stay in courts — vernacular preaching was their strength.
xa: Other limitation: **Naqshbandi orthodoxy** pushed back against Sufi-Bhakti liberalism.
Criticism: **egalitarian preaching did not dismantle caste**.

49.s:
With reference to the religious history of medieval India, the Sufi mystics were known to pursue which of the following practices?
1. Meditation and control of breath
2. Severe ascetic exercises in a lonely place
3. Recitation of holy songs to arouse a state of ecstasy in their audience
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
49.x: Sufi mystics emphasised internal purification and self-awareness, often practising meditation and breath control as part of their spiritual discipline. These practices were adapted to focus on the remembrance of God (Zikr) and achieving a state of divine connection. Many Sufi saints engaged in ascetic practices, often withdrawing to isolated places for meditation and contemplation. This detachment from worldly pleasures was intended to focus entirely on God. Sufis are well known for their practice of Sama, which involves reciting or singing devotional songs and poetry. This was done to evoke a state of spiritual ecstasy and divine love, for both themselves and their followers.

49.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the interaction between Nath yogis and Sufis?
o: Hath-yogic techniques influenced some Sufi practices
It was confined exclusively to temple rituals
Sufis adopted certain yogic meditation practices
49.x: The interaction involved dialogues, meditation and breath control; it was not confined to temple rituals.
xa: **Amritakund** was translated into **Arabic and Persian in the 13th century**.
It gave Sufis **breath control** in all orders except the **Naqshbandis**.

49.s: Which Sufi equated 'Alakh Niranjan' with 'Khuda' in Hindi verse?
49.x: Hamiduddin Nagori equated the Nath term 'Alakh Niranjan' with 'Khuda' in Hindi verse. Nizamuddin Auliya noted the yogic Siva-Sakti division of the body, Ahmad Sirhindi was an orthodox Naqshbandi, and Bahauddin Zakariya was a Suhrawardi close to the court.
xs: **Hamiduddin Nagori** equated **'Alakh Niranjan'** with **'Khuda'** in Hindi verse — option **(2)** is correct.
**Nizamuddin Auliya** noted the **Siva-Sakti** division; **Ahmad Sirhindi** was the orthodox **Naqshbandi** reaction.
xa: **Dara Shikoh** (Qadiri) carried forward the **syncretic line**.
**Sheikh Nuruddin** founded the **Rishi movement** (Kashmir).

49.s: The Nathpanthi tradition of Hath Yoga is particularly associated with which of the following figures?
49.x: The Kanphata Yogis followed the Nath tradition of Gorakhnath and were practitioners of Hath Yoga.
49.tq: Apply the founder-or-associated-person trap by separating Nath yogis from Sufi figures.
xs: Nathpanthi Hath Yoga belongs to the **Kanphata** yogis of **Gorakhnath's** Nath tradition — option **(4) Gorakhnath**.
**Hamiduddin Nagori** equated **'Alakh Niranjan'** with 'Khuda'; **Faqirullah** wrote **Raga Darpan**; **Amir Khusrau** introduced the **Qaul**.
xa: **Kanphata** = split-eared yogis.
Sufis adopted Hath-yogic techniques (UPPSC 2019: **both statements correct**).

49.s: Which one of the following statements about Nizamuddin Auliya and yogic ideas is correct?
o: He was struck by the yogic division of the body into Siva and Sakti.
He founded the Nathpanthi order at Ajmer.
He rejected all knowledge of Nath yogic practices.
He translated Amritakund into Persian during the 13th century.
49.x: Nizamuddin Auliya noted the yogic division of the body: Siva from the head to the navel and Sakti below the navel.
49.tq: Match the specific observation with the correct religious personality.
xs: **Nizamuddin Auliya** noted the yogic division of the body into **Siva** (head to navel) and **Sakti** (below navel) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Amritakund** was translated in the **13th century**, but the notes do not credit Nizamuddin with it.
xa: **Alberuni** noted Sufi parallels with the **Yoga Sutra** and **Bhagavad Gita**.
**Hamiduddin Nagori** equated **'Alakh Niranjan'** with **'Khuda'**.

49.s: Hath Yoga, whose techniques some Sufis adopted, was practised by the:
49.x: Hath Yoga was practised by the Nathpanthi yogis of Gorakhnath's tradition, and Sufis adopted techniques such as breath control.
xa: The **Naqshbandis** were the exception to breath control.
Nath yogis and Sufis held **spiritual dialogues**.

49.s: Which Sufi order did NOT adopt yogic breath control?
49.x: After the Amritakund was translated, breath control was adopted in all orders except the Naqshbandis.

49.s: The Hath-yogic text translated into Arabic and Persian in the 13th century was the:
49.x: The Amritakund, a Hath-yogic text, was rendered into Arabic and Persian in the 13th century.

49.s: The Nathpanth tradition is traced to:
49.x: The Nathpanth goes back to Matsyendranath; Gorakhnath and the Kanphata yogis practised Hath Yoga.
