78.x: The Government of India Act, 1919 made a major change in Provincial governance. The Government of India Act, 1919 introduced the system of Dyarchy. Dyarchy means a dual set of Governments. The Government of India Act of 1919, made a provision for classification of the central and provincial subjects. The provincial subjects were divided into two groups: one was Reserved and another was Transferred. The Reserved subjects were kept with the Governor and his executive council and transferred subjects were handed over to the Minister responsible to the provincial legislature. This division of subjects was basically what they meant by introducing the Dyarchy.

74.s: Indigo cultivation in India declined by the beginning of the 20 th century because of
o: Peasant resistance to the oppressive conduct of planters
Its unprofitability in the world market because of new inventions
National leaders' opposition to the cultivation of Indigo
74.x: The decline of indigo cultivation in India in the early 20 th century was primarily driven by the advent of synthetic dyes, particularly synthetic indigo. By the end of the 19 th century, synthetic dyes had become widely available, drastically reducing the demand for natural indigo. Traditionally, indigo was a natural dye extracted from certain plants, and India had been a major producer of indigo for the global market. Synthetic dyes offered cost-effective alternatives and could be produced in larger quantities, making them more attractive to manufacturers. As a result, the market for natural indigo became unprofitable, leading to a decline in its cultivation in India.

74.s: The first venture of Gandhi in all India politics was the:
74.x: Champaran (1917), Kheda (1918), Ahmedabad (1918) — were localised movements addressing peasants' and workers' grievances. The Rowlatt Satyagraha (1919), against the repressive Rowlatt Act, was Gandhi's first all-India political campaign. He organised the Satyagraha Sabha and called for a nationwide hartal on April 6, 1919, marking his emergence as a national leader. The Non-Cooperation Movement (1920) was larger in scale but came later, not as his first venture into all-India politics.

74.s: The first venture of Gandhi in all-India politics was the:
74.x: Every movement started by Gandhiji helped Indian Nationalism to attain an unprecedented height. The Movements conceived by Gandhiji like Champaran Peasant Movement (1917 A.D.), Ahmedabad Mill Workers Movement (1918 A.D.), Kheda Peasant Movement(1918 A.D.) were limited to the specific issue of a particular section of the society. The scope of the area was also very limited. But Rowlatt Satyagraha (1919 A.D.) against the censure of freedom of press and detention without trial was proactively joined by all the sections of the society. Sentiments of the aggrieved common people were addressed. Knitting of people from all religions, all castes, all age groups, and both the genders in the Nationalist Movement had a distinguished characteristic of the Rowlatt Satyagraha. National newspapers, political journals, etc. made Gandhi a popular figure. This was the first all India level Movement launched by Mahatma Gandhi.

Campaign for the Release: In its Bombay session in September 1945, the All India Congress Committee (AICC) declared its support for the INA soldiers. The Congress established the INA Defence Committee to defend the INA prisoners. It included famous lawyers such as Bhulabhai Desai, M. Asaf Ali, Tej Bahadur Sapru, K.N. Katju, and Jawaharlal Nehru. In addition to legal help, Congress organised relief funds and arranged employment for the INA men. There was a countrywide protest against the trial of three INA heroes (Sehgal, Shah Nawaz and Dhillon) belonging to the Modern Indian History PMF IAS IH – 126 Hindu, Muslim and Sikh communities, symbolising the unity of the people. The Commander-in-Chief, Claude Auchinleck, was forced to remit the sentences due to prevailing circumstances. Later, all three defendants were released. This case became a symbol of the country's freedom struggle and showed the strength of Unity.

80.s: On which date did the Nizam and the Government of India sign the Standstill Agreement?
80.x:
The Standstill Agreement between the Government of India and the Nizam of Hyderabad was signed on 29 November 1947. The agreement was intended to maintain the existing administrative, economic and communication arrangements between Hyderabad State and the Dominion of India for one year while negotiations regarding Hyderabad's future continued. However, the Nizam continued efforts to remain independent, leading to increasing political unrest. The issue was finally resolved through Operation Polo (Police Action) in September 1948, resulting in the integration of Hyderabad into the Indian Union. Hence, the correct answer is Option (3).
Exam Note:
• Standstill Agreement – 29 November 1947
• Parties – Government of India & Nizam of Hyderabad

Constituent Assembly (1946) *The early non-official draft of Constituent Assembly was enshrined in Swaraj Bill of 1895, which was influenced by Bal Gangadhar Tilak’s directions. In the 20th century, Gandhiji firstly pointed towards this idea when in the year 1922 AD he said that the Indian Constitution should be made as per India’s need. On February 8, 1924, Motilal Nehru officially introduced a resolution in the Central Legislative Assembly, known as the 'National Demand' calling for a round table conference to establish a constitution-making body, marking a pivotal early demand for a Constituent Assembly. After this M.N. Roy proposed this demand and the basic concepts of Constituent Assembly was reiterated by Jawahar Lal Nehru. Congress in Faizpur Session (December 1936 AD) reaffirmed the idea of the Constituent Assembly and also pointed out its importance. Constituent Assembly was formed on the recommendation of the Cabinet Mission Plan. *On 24 March, 1946 AD, Cabinet Mission arrived at Delhi. 104.s: Which one of the following statements is incorrect regarding the Andhra Mahasabha?
o: It was founded in 1930 at Jogipet.
Madapati Hanumantha Rao was its first President.
It played a significant role in spreading education and political awareness among the people of Telangana.
It was established primarily to support the policies of the Nizam Government.
104.x:
The Andhra Mahasabha was founded in 1930 at Jogipet (Medak district) with the objective of promoting the social, educational and cultural advancement of Telugu-speaking people in the Hyderabad State. The first session was presided over by Madapati Hanumantha Rao, who is popularly known as the "Andhra Pitamaha." Initially, the organisation concentrated on social reforms, promotion of the Telugu language and expansion of education. Gradually, it developed into an important political platform that opposed the autocratic rule of the Nizam and spread political consciousness among the people of Telangana. During the 1940s, many of its leaders became associated with the peasant movement against feudal oppression. Therefore, the statement that it was established to support the policies of the Nizam Government is incorrect. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Founded – 1930
• Place – Jogipet (Medak)
• First President – Madapati Hanumantha Rao
• Objective – Social reform, education and political awareness among Telugu people of Hyderabad State

Andhra University is the first university established exclusively for Telugu-speaking people. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).

104.s: Andhra State was formed on
104.x:
Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953 by separating the Telugu-speaking districts from the erstwhile Madras State. It became the first linguistic state to be created in independent India. The formation of Andhra State was the culmination of a long struggle for a separate Telugu-speaking province. The movement reached its peak after the fast unto death by Potti Sreeramulu, who sacrificed his life on 15 December 1952 demanding a separate Andhra State. His martyrdom led to widespread protests, compelling the Government of India to accept the demand. Kurnool became the capital of the newly formed Andhra State, while the High Court was established at Guntur. Later, on 1 November 1956, Andhra State was merged with the Telugu-speaking districts of Hyderabad State to form Andhra Pradesh under the States Reorganisation Act. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).
Exam Note:
• Andhra State – 1 October 1953
• First Linguistic State in Independent India
• Capital – Kurnool
• High Court – Guntur

104.s: Arrange the following in chronological order: A. Formation of the Visalandra Mahasabha B. Dhar Commission C. Swami Sitaram's fast D. Formation of States Re-organization Commission
104.x:
The demand for a separate Andhra State and later a Visalandhra gained momentum after Independence through a series of political developments. The Dhar Commission was appointed in 1948 to examine the question of linguistic provinces. It did not recommend the formation of states on a linguistic basis. In 1949, the Visalandra Mahasabha was formed to campaign for the unification of all Telugu-speaking areas into a single state. Swami Sitaram undertook his fast in 1951 demanding the formation of Andhra State, which further intensified the movement. The States Reorganisation Commission (SRC) was constituted in 1953 under the chairmanship of Justice Fazl Ali to examine the reorganisation of states on linguistic and administrative grounds. Its recommendations eventually led to the formation of Andhra Pradesh on 1 November 1956. Thus, the correct chronological order is: Dhar Commission → Visalandra Mahasabha → Swami Sitaram's Fast → States Reorganisation Commission Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• Dhar Commission – 1948
• Visalandra Mahasabha – 1949
• Swami Sitaram's Fast – 1951
• States Reorganisation Commission – 1953

105.s: According to the Gentlemen's Agreement, what was the ratio of Cabinet representation for Andhra and Telangana?
105.x:
The Gentlemen's Agreement, signed in 1956 before the formation of Andhra Pradesh, was intended to safeguard the interests of the Telangana region after its merger with Andhra State. One of its important provisions related to the composition of the State Cabinet. It provided that the Cabinet should consist of ministers in the ratio of 60:40 between Andhra and Telangana, reflecting the relative population of the two regions while ensuring adequate representation for Telangana. The Agreement also included safeguards relating to public employment, expenditure, education and the establishment of the Telangana Regional Committee. Therefore, the correct answer is Option (3).

• Cabinet Ratio – 60 : 40

At the time of the party's formation, Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy was the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh. He served as Chief Minister from 24 February 1982 to 20 September 1982. Within a short period of its formation, the Telugu Desam Party achieved a historic victory in the 1983 Andhra Pradesh Assembly Elections, bringing N. T. Rama Rao to power. Hence, the correct answer is Option (3).

82.s: How did the Jai Andhra Movement end in 1972–73?
o: With the abolition of Mulki Rules
With the arrests of many student and women leaders
As the Central forces suppressed the movement
With the Six-Point Formula proposed by the Central Government
82.x:
The Jai Andhra Movement (1972–73) emerged in the Andhra region in response to the implementation of the Mulki Rules, which gave preference to local candidates in public employment in Telangana. The movement demanded either the abolition of the Mulki Rules or the creation of a separate Andhra State. It witnessed widespread protests, demonstrations and political instability. To resolve the regional tensions, the Central Government introduced the Six-Point Formula in 1973. The formula aimed to ensure balanced regional development, provide equitable opportunities in education and employment, and reduce regional disparities. It eventually replaced the earlier safeguards and brought the movement to an end. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).

• Ended with – Six-Point Formula (1973)
• Objective – Regional balance and employment safeguards

Many people in the Andhra region viewed the judgment as discriminatory, leading to widespread protests demanding either the abolition of the Mulki Rules or the creation of a separate Andhra State. The movement ultimately led to the Six-Point Formula (1973) as a political solution. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).

82.s: The Six-Point Formula came into force through this Constitutional Amendment?
82.x:
The Six-Point Formula, evolved in 1973 to resolve the regional issues arising from the Jai Andhra Movement and the Telangana Movement, was given constitutional protection through the 32nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1973. The amendment inserted Article 371D and Article 371E into the Constitution, enabling special provisions relating to public employment, education and administrative arrangements in Andhra Pradesh. Article 371D provided for equitable opportunities and facilities for people belonging to different regions of the State in matters of public employment and education. Hence, the correct answer is Option (3).
Exam Note:
• Constitutional Amendment – 32nd Amendment Act, 1973
• Inserted – Articles 371D & 371E
• Purpose – Implementation of Six-Point Formula

82.s: The Six Points Formula came into effect under the Constitutional Amendment of:
82.x: 32nd Amendment The Six Point Formula, aimed at addressing regional imbalances between Andhra and Telangana, came into effect under the 32nd Constitutional Amendment. This amendment gave constitutional backing to safeguards for Telangana's development and employment. It remained a key reference point in later Telangana-related political debates.

106.s: Land consolidation succeeded particularly in:

shielded zamindari abolition measures from legal challenge

Tenancy reform was defeated by **"voluntary surrenders"**.

106.s: Which approach to tribal policy was favoured by Jawaharlal Nehru over both isolation and forced assimilation?

106.s: Dadra and Nagar Haveli was freed in 1954 and subsequently made a Union Territory by which Constitutional Amendment?
106.x: The Tenth Amendment Act of 1961 made Dadra and Nagar Haveli a Union Territory.
106.tq: Match the territory with the correct Constitutional Amendment.
xs: **Dadra & Nagar Haveli** was made a UT by the **10th Amendment, 1961** — option **(1)**.
**12th Amendment, 1962** = **Goa**; **14th Amendment, 1962** = **Pondicherry**.
xa: Dadra & Nagar Haveli was **freed in 1954**.
Goa was taken by **Operation Vijay**, **18-19 Dec 1961**.
Goa became a full state in **1987**.

106.s: NEFA, which is now known as Arunachal Pradesh, was administered initially through the:
106.x: NEFA was run through the Governor of Assam and served as a policy laboratory for Elwin's approach.
106.tq: Test the administrative authority associated with a former regional name.
xs: **NEFA** was run through the **Governor of Assam** — option **(3)**.
It was a **policy laboratory** for **Elwin's** approach.
xa: NEFA became a UT in **1972** and a state in **1987**.
**Verrier Elwin** wrote **A Philosophy for NEFA**.
⚠ **1987** = Arunachal **and** Goa statehood.

106.s: The Centre responded to the Naga question in 1963 principally by granting:
o: Sixth Schedule status to the whole of Assam
106.x: The Centre addressed the Naga question in 1963 by creating the state of Nagaland. The demand for Greater Nagalim associated with the NSCN continued thereafter.
106.tq: Distinguish the actual constitutional response from the continuing political demand.
xs: The Centre answered the **Naga National Council** by granting **statehood to Nagaland** in **1963** — option **(1)**.
Nagaland got **full statehood**, not UT status; independence was **not** granted.
xa: The **Greater Nagalim** demand (**NSCN**) continues.
NNC was led by **A.Z. Phizo**.

106.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the integration of the French and Portuguese enclaves?
o: Pondicherry was transferred to India by the French in 1954
Goa became a full-fledged State in 1961
Goa, Daman and Diu were liberated in 1961
Pondicherry became a Union Territory in 1962
106.x: Goa was liberated in 1961 but attained statehood only in 1987; the other dates are correct.

106.s: Goa became a full-fledged State through the:
106.x: Goa became a State by the 56th Amendment (1987); the 12th made it a UT.

106.s: Before it was freed in 1954, Dadra and Nagar Haveli was a ____ possession.
106.x: Dadra and Nagar Haveli was Portuguese, never French.

106.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about border consolidation?
o: Dadra and Nagar Haveli became a UT by the 10th Amendment
NEFA became the State of Arunachal Pradesh in 1972
Goa, Daman and Diu became a UT by the 12th Amendment
Pondicherry became a UT by the 14th Amendment

106.s: The Vibrant Villages Programme-II covers how many border villages?
106.x: VVP-II covers 1,954 border villages in 15 States and 2 UTs.

106.s: The National Integration Council was set up in 1961 by Jawaharlal Nehru after the:
106.x: The National Integration Council was established by Nehru in 1961 after the National Integration Conference.
106.tq: Link the institution to its immediate constitutional-political origin.
xs: **Nehru** set up the **National Integration Council** in **1961** after the **National Integration Conference** — option **(1)**.
The Conference addressed **communalism, casteism, regionalism and linguism**.
xa: Other tools vs regionalism: **Art. 44**, **Art. 51A**, the **Fifth, Sixth and Eighth Schedules**.
**Anti-Hindi agitations in Tamil Nadu (1937, 1965, 1986)** → **two-language formula**.
Nehru's tribal policy was **integration**.

106.s: The AP Official Languages Act, which made Telugu the official language of the State, was passed in:
106.x: The AP Official Languages Act, 1966 made Telugu the State's official language.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about national integration and language:
1. The National Integration Council was set up in 1961 by Jawaharlal Nehru.
2. The AP Official Languages Act made Telugu the official language of the State.
3. The National Integration Council was set up by Lal Bahadur Shastri.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: Nehru set up the NIC in 1961, and the 1966 Official Languages Act made Telugu official; Shastri did not set it up.

106.s: Who was the social reformer mainly responsible for the disappearance of " Bhogam " caste from Andhra Society?
106.x: Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu was the social reformer principally responsible for the disappearance of the ' Bhogam ' (devadasi) caste tradition from Andhra society. He campaigned actively against the devadasi system as part of broader social reform efforts. His work contributed to changing attitudes on this practice in early 20th-century Andhra.

106.s: The raising of the BC reservation in Andhra Pradesh to 44% in 1986 was based on the report of the:
106.x: The Muralidhar Rao Commission (1982) led to NTR raising the BC quota to 44% in 1986, later struck down by the High Court. The Subba Rao Committee was behind the AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act 1956; the Prakasam Committee (1938) recommended abolition of intermediaries; the Kumarappa Committee (1949) set the land-reform agenda.
106.tq: BC 44% (1986) = Muralidhar Rao Commission (1982), NTR; struck down by HC.
xs: The **44%** BC quota (**1986**) followed the **Muralidhar Rao Commission** (**1982**) — option **(1)**.
**Subba Rao Committee** → **Andhra Area Tenancy Act, 1956**; **Prakasam Committee (1938)** → abolition of intermediaries; **Kumarappa Committee** (**1949**) → land-reform agenda.
xa: The **High Court** struck down the raised quota.
Backward Muslims got **4%** (**BC-E**) in **2007**.
**Art. 371D** gives local-cadre reservation in jobs and education.

106.s: Article 371D, which implemented the Six-Point Formula, was inserted by the:
106.x: The Six-Point Formula of 1973 was implemented through Article 371D, inserted by the 32nd Constitutional Amendment in 1973.
xa: **Muralidhar Rao Commission** (**1982**) → BC quota **44%** (**1986**), struck down by the High Court.
**4%** reservation for backward Muslims (**BC-E**): **2007**.
Nehru's **NIC** (**1961**) was another integration tool.

106.s: Backward Muslims in Andhra Pradesh were given a 4% quota under the category:
106.x: Backward Muslims got 4% reservation under BC-E, introduced in 2007.
xa: The **44%** quota followed the **Muralidhar Rao Commission** (**1982**) and was **struck down by the High Court**.
**Art. 371D** (**32nd Amendment, 1973**) gives local-cadre reservation.
The **Six-Point Formula** is of **1973**.

106.s: The Madras Devadasi (Prevention of Dedication) Act of December 1947 was piloted by:
106.x: The Act was piloted by Muthulakshmi Reddy; Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu was a reformer who campaigned against the Bhogam system.
xa: The **AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act** came in **1988**.
It also covers **Jogini, Basivi, Matangi** dedication.
**Dubagunta (Nellore)** women's anti-arrack movement: **1992**.

106.s: Which of the following practices were also covered by the Andhra Pradesh Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1988?
106.x: The 1988 Act also covered Jogini, Basivi and Matangi forms of dedication.
106.tq: Recall the complete group of practices covered by the legislation.
xs: The **1988** AP Act also covers **Jogini, Basivi and Matangi** dedication — option **(4)**.
**Jagir, Sarfekhas, Inam**, **Ryotwari, Zamindari, Diwani** are land-tenure terms, not forms of dedication.
xa: The **Madras** Act (**December 1947**) was piloted by **Muthulakshmi Reddy**.
**Bhogam** is another name for the Devadasi system.
**Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu** campaigned against it.

106.s: Total prohibition was introduced in Andhra Pradesh under N.T. Rama Rao in:
106.x: Total prohibition came in 1995, after the Dubagunta movement (1992) and the arrack ban (1993); it was lifted in 1997.
xa: Dubagunta is in **Nellore**.
NTR also launched the **Rs 2 per kg rice** scheme (**1983**).
Chandrababu Naidu also launched **Janmabhoomi** (**1997**).

106.x: Rajasthan adopted Panchayati Raj on 2 October 1959; AP followed on 1 November 1959.

106.x: The 1986 Act under NTR replaced Panchayat Samitis with Mandal Praja Parishads.

106.x: Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy banned arrack in 1993; NTR brought total prohibition in 1995.

106.x: Dubagunta, the village of the 1992 anti-arrack movement, is in Nellore.

106.s: Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu campaigned against the:
106.x: Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu campaigned against the Bhogam system.

106.s: Total prohibition, introduced in 1995, was lifted in Andhra Pradesh in:
106.x: NTR's 1995 total prohibition was lifted by Chandrababu Naidu in 1997.

106.s: Which of the following scheme – Chief Minister – year sets is correctly matched?
o: Rs 2 per kg rice scheme – N.T. Rama Rao – 1983
106.x: The Rs 2 per kg rice scheme, with subsidised housing and Janata cloth, was introduced by N.T. Rama Rao in 1983.

106.s: The first residential school in Andhra Pradesh (1971) was set up at:
106.x: The first residential school was set up at Sarvail in Nalgonda district in 1971, under P.V. Narasimha Rao.
xa: PVNR (CM **1971-73**) also had the AP Cabinet pass the **Land Reforms Bill**.

106.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Fee Reimbursement — higher education of poor students — 2008
Rajiv Aarogyasri — health insurance for the poor — 2007
Janmabhoomi — health insurance for the poor — 1997
106.x: Janmabhoomi concerned people's participation in development, not health insurance. Indiramma, Rajiv Aarogyasri and Fee Reimbursement are correctly matched with their purposes and years.

xs: **Janmabhoomi — health insurance** is NOT correctly matched — option **(4)**; Janmabhoomi (**1997**) = **people's participation in development**.
Health insurance for the poor = **Rajiv Aarogyasri** (**2007**).
The rest are right: **Fee Reimbursement 2008**, **Indiramma housing 2006**.
xa: Janmabhoomi was **N. Chandrababu Naidu**'s scheme.
Indiramma, Aarogyasri and Fee Reimbursement were **Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy**'s.
**Rs 2 per kg rice**: **NTR**, **1983**.

106.s: Which institution was the first open university in India?
o: Andhra Pradesh Open University, now Dr B.R. Ambedkar Open University
106.x: The Andhra Pradesh Open University, now named Dr B.R. Ambedkar Open University, was the first open university in India and was established in 1982.

xs: India's first open university was the **AP Open University**, now **Dr B.R. Ambedkar Open University** (**1982**) — option **(4)**.
**Telugu University** = **1985**; **Nagarjuna** and **Kakatiya** = **1976**.

xs: **NTR University of Health Sciences** (**1986**) was India's first health university — option **(4)**.
**Dr B.R. Ambedkar Open University** was the first **open** university (**1982**).
xa: **Nagarjuna** (Guntur) and **Kakatiya** (Warangal): **1976**.
**Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University**: **1985**.

106.x: Aarogyasri dates from 2007; Indiramma was 2006 and Fee Reimbursement 2008.

106.s: Dr. Y. S. Rajasekhara Reddy lost his life in the tragic helicopter accident on?
106.x:
Dr. Yeduguri Sandinti Rajasekhara Reddy (Y. S. R.), the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, died in a helicopter crash in the Nallamala Forest. Although the helicopter went missing on 2 September 2009, the wreckage was located and his death was officially confirmed on 5 September 2009. His tenure is remembered for several flagship welfare schemes including Aarogyasri, Jalayagnam, Indiramma Housing and Fee Reimbursement. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• Helicopter Crash – 2 September 2009
• Death Confirmed – 5 September 2009
• Chief Minister – Dr. Y. S. Rajasekhara Reddy

106.s: In which year was Janmabhoomi (a rural development programme) launched in Andhra Pradesh?
In which State was the Bhoodan Movement first started?
106.x: Acharya Vinoba Bhave on April 18, 1951 A.D. started the Bhoodan Movement from Pochampalli in Andhra Pradesh (Now Telangana). It was an attempt at land reform and institutional change in agriculture. Jaya Prakash Narayan, leaving active politics joined Bhoodan Movement in 1954 A.D.
